title: A compatible finite Galois polynomial envelope for a nonfaithful field action
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $H$ a finite group with an action $A:H\to\operatorname{Aut}(K)$ by field automorphisms, not necessarily faithful. Put $H_0=A(H)$ and $F=K^{H_0}=\{x\in K:A_h(x)=x\text{ for every }h\in H\}$. Let $I$ be a finite set, possibly empty, and let $f_i\in K[T]$ be monic of degree $d_i\ge1$. For each $i$, suppose given a nonempty finite set $B_i$, finite separable extensions $K_{ib}/K$, and a $K$-algebra isomorphism $K[T]/(f_i)\cong\prod_{b\in B_i}K_{ib}$. Then there exists an extension $M\supseteq K\supseteq F$ such that $M/F$ and $M/K$ are finite Galois and there are $K$-embeddings $K_{ib}\hookrightarrow M$ for every $i,b$. Each polynomial has a complete linear factorization $f_i(T)=\prod_{\nu=1}^{d_i}(T-\beta_{i\nu})$ in $M[T]$. For this $M$ the set
$$J=\{(h,\sigma)\in H\times\operatorname{Aut}_F(M):\sigma|_K=A_h\}$$
is a finite group with componentwise multiplication, and $\rho:J\to H$, $(h,\sigma)\mapsto h$, is surjective. The second projection gives an action of $J$ on $M$ extending $A$ through $\rho$. For $N=\ker\rho$, the map $(1,\sigma)\mapsto\sigma$ identifies $N$ with $\operatorname{Aut}_K(M)$ and $M^N=K$. The subfield $K$ is the specified embedded copy, so every embedding asserted above fixes that copy pointwise.

Fields, extensions, towers and polynomial rings use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-field-tower] and [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Finite Galois means finite-dimensional, separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and normal: every element's minimal polynomial splits into linear factors. Superscripts denote elements fixed by all automorphisms in the indicated group.

proof.text: The image $H_0=A(H)$ is finite and acts faithfully on $K$ by its inclusion into $\operatorname{Aut}(K)$. Its fixed field is precisely the stated $F$, since asking that every element of the image fix $x$ is equivalent to asking that every $A_h$ fix $x$. Apply [lem-wf-finite-field-action-fixed-degree] to $H_0$ and $K$: $K/F$ is finite Galois. No faithfulness of $A$ on $H$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 09I3, lemma-galois-over-fixed-field; apply to the image of the action.

proof.text: For each $(i,b)$, separable transitivity [lem-zl-separable-permanence] applied to $F\subseteq K\subseteq K_{ib}$ gives separability of $K_{ib}/F$. This extension is finite: if $(u_s)$ spans $K/F$ and $(v_t)$ spans $K_{ib}/K$, then the finitely many $u_sv_t$ span $K_{ib}/F$, by expanding each coefficient of $\sum_t c_tv_t$ in the $u_s$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions] over $F$ to the finite family consisting of $K$ and all $K_{ib}$. It supplies a finite Galois extension $M/F$, an $F$-embedding $j:K\hookrightarrow M$, and $F$-embeddings $e_{ib}:K_{ib}\hookrightarrow M$. Always include $K$ in this family, even when $I$ is empty. Equip $M$ with its $K$-extension structure through $j$; henceforth $K\subseteq M$ denotes this specified copy.

source.place: Tags 09HB, lemma-separable-permanence; 09DT, lemma-normal-closure; 0EXM, lemma-normal-closure-galois; finite spanning-set calculation.

proof.text: The $e_{ib}$ need not initially be $K$-linear. Write $a_{ib}:K\hookrightarrow M$ for their restrictions. The map $\tau_{ib}:a_{ib}(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}j(K)$ defined by $a_{ib}(x)\mapsto j(x)$ is an $F$-isomorphism between subfields of $M$. Both contain the same image of $F$. Since $M/F$ is algebraic normal, [lem-sfb-normal-intermediate-isomorphism-lifts] extends $\tau_{ib}$ to an $F$-automorphism $s_{ib}$ of $M$. Then $u_{ib}=s_{ib}\circ e_{ib}$ is a field embedding with $u_{ib}(x)=j(x)$ for every $x\in K$. These are the required $K$-embeddings. This argument does not identify different copies of $K$ without a comparison map.

source.place: Tag 0BME, lemma-lift-maps (2), applied to the isomorphism between the two embedded copies of K.

proof.text: Apply [lem-dl-a1-galois-over-intermediate] to $F\subseteq K\subseteq M$. It gives that $M/K$ is separable algebraic and normal. An $F$-spanning set of $M$ also spans $M$ over $K$, since $F\subseteq K$, so $M/K$ is finite. Thus both $M/F$ and $M/K$ are finite Galois, with the original structure map $j$ on $K$.

source.place: Tag 09I2, lemma-galois-goes-up, and the elementary spanning-set observation of lemma-finite-goes-up.

proof.text: Fix $i$. Let $t_{ib}\in K_{ib}$ be the $b$th coordinate of the image of $T$ under the given isomorphism $K[T]/(f_i)\cong\prod_b K_{ib}$, and let $m_{ib}\in K[T]$ be its minimal polynomial. The minimal-polynomial definition [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] gives $m_{ib}(t_{ib})=0$. The polynomial $P_i=\prod_b m_{ib}$ therefore vanishes at every coordinate $t_{ib}$. Its class in the product algebra, hence in $K[T]/(f_i)$, is zero. By the definition of the quotient by $(f_i)$, this means $P_i=f_iq_i$ for some $q_i\in K[T]$. Each $m_{ib}$ is also the minimal polynomial of $u_{ib}(t_{ib})$ in $M$: the embedding $u_{ib}$ fixes $K$, so a polynomial evaluates to zero before applying it if and only if it evaluates to zero afterwards. Normality of $M/K$ now makes every $m_{ib}$ a product of linear factors in $M[T]$; concatenating these products makes the monic nonzero $P_i$ split there. Apply [lem-trf-divisor-of-split-polynomial] in the field $M$ to $f_i\mid P_i$. It gives $f_i=c\prod_{\nu=1}^{n_i}(T-\beta_{i\nu})$. Leading coefficients give $c=1$ because $f_i$ is monic. Degrees then give $n_i=d_i$, the required complete factorization. This argument allows repeated roots; no squarefreeness inference is needed.

source.place: Tag 09HN, lemma-normal-goes-up, proof: divisors of split polynomials split; section-normal (09HL), normality meaning. Quotient-kernel calculation written by Q16.

proof.text: Define $J$ as in the statement. It contains $(1,\mathrm{id}_M)$. For compatible pairs $(h,\sigma)$ and $(g,\tau)$ and $x\in K$, one has $\sigma\tau(j(x))=\sigma(j(A_g(x)))=j(A_hA_g(x))=j(A_{hg}(x))$. Thus their product is compatible. The equation $\sigma\circ j=j\circ A_h$ implies $\sigma^{-1}\circ j=j\circ A_{h^{-1}}$, proving closure under inverses. Hence $J$ is a subgroup of $H\times\operatorname{Aut}_F(M)$, and its projections are homomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field], applied to $M/F$, the second factor is finite. Since $H$ is finite, $J$ is finite. The second projection acts on $M$ by field automorphisms, and compatibility gives exactly its asserted restriction to $K$.

source.place: Tag 09I1, lemma-finite-Galois, finiteness; elementary compatible-pair subgroup and action calculations, elaborating de Jong Lemma 5.6.

proof.text: Every $A_h$ fixes $F$ by its definition. On the embedded subfield $K$ it is therefore an $F$-automorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-intermediate-isomorphism-lifts] with ambient extension $M/F$ and both intermediate subfields equal to $K$. It gives $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_F(M)$ extending $A_h$. Consequently $(h,\sigma)\in J$ and $\rho(h,\sigma)=h$. This proves that $\rho$ is surjective, including when distinct elements of $H$ induce the same field automorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BME, lemma-lift-maps (2); extend A_h over the fixed base F.

proof.text: An element of $N=\ker\rho$ has first coordinate $1$. Its compatibility equation is $\sigma\circ j=j$, which says precisely that $\sigma$ fixes $K$ pointwise. Conversely every $K$-automorphism of $M$ fixes $F$ and yields $(1,\sigma)\in N$. The maps $(1,\sigma)\mapsto\sigma$ and $\sigma\mapsto(1,\sigma)$ are inverse group homomorphisms. Under the second-projection action, being fixed by $N$ is therefore equivalent to being fixed by every $K$-automorphism of $M$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] to the finite Galois extension $M/K$ from step 4. Its fixed-field clause gives $M^N=j(K)$, written $K$ with our fixed embedding. All the $u_{ib}$ from step 3 fix this same embedded copy, completing every clause.
